records.text: He bottled it at the last minute and threw his colleagues under the bus.

artifact.comprehensible: At the very last moment, he lost his nerve and betrayed his colleagues by shifting the blame onto them.

glosses.gloss: lost his nerve and failed to do what he was supposed to do

glosses.expression: threw his colleagues under the bus
glosses.gloss: betrayed his colleagues or put them in trouble to protect himself

artifact.translation: 彼は土壇場で怖じ気づき、同僚を犠牲にして自分を守った。

records.text: The house stood in a state of genteel decay, its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent.

artifact.comprehensible: The house was in a condition of respectable, upper-class decline, because the people who lived there had moved away to mainland Europe a long time ago.

glosses.gloss: a state of decline that still keeps a respectable, upper-class appearance
having moved to (a place) a long time ago; 'repaired to' is a formal, old-fashioned way of saying 'went to'
mainland Europe (used especially by British speakers)

artifact.grammar: The phrase 'its occupants having long since repaired to the Continent' is a participle clause that gives the reason for the house's decay. It has no finite verb ('having repaired' is a participle), so it cannot stand alone as a sentence; it attaches to the main clause 'The house stood in a state of genteel decay' and explains why.
artifact.translation: その家は、上品な荒れ方をした状態で建っていた。住人たちはずっと前にヨーロッパ大陸へ移り住んでいたからだ。

records.text: The lessee shall indemnify the lessor against all claims arising from any breach of the covenants herein.

artifact.comprehensible: The person renting the property must protect the owner from any claims that come from breaking any of the promises in this agreement.

glosses.gloss: to protect someone from loss or damage by paying for it or taking legal responsibility
the person who rents something (the tenant)
the person who owns and rents out something (the landlord)
formal promises or agreements, especially in a legal document

artifact.translation: 賃借人は、本契約に定める約束の違反から生じるすべての請求に対して、賃貸人を補償しなければならない。

records.text: It behoves us to consider whether such a course of action is consonant with our obligations.

artifact.comprehensible: It is proper for us to think about whether acting in that way fits with what we are obliged to do.

glosses.gloss: is right or proper for (someone) to do
that way of acting; that plan

artifact.grammar: The sentence uses a formal pattern: 'It behoves us to consider...' means 'It is proper for us to consider...'. The 'it' is a placeholder subject, and the real subject is the infinitive phrase 'to consider...'. The clause 'whether such a course of action is consonant with our obligations' is the object of 'consider'.
artifact.translation: そのような行動が我々の義務と一致するかどうかを考えることは、我々にとってふさわしいことである。
